title: RevisionOrchestrator Service — Autonomous Multi-Pass Revision Engine
description: Create a backend service that autonomously revises text through multiple evaluate→revise→verify passes with configurable quality gates, convergence detection, and checkpoint-based safety. Register new MCP endpoint /agent/revise-multi-pass.
action: Create src-ts/src/agents/revision-orchestrator.ts with RevisionOrchestrator class. Create src-ts/src/mcp/endpoints/revision-orchestrator.ts with POST /agent/revise-multi-pass endpoint. The orchestrator manages a text buffer in memory, calls existing evaluation (via /agent/context with module='evaluation'), uses the revision API to generate improved text, and loops until target_score is reached or max_iterations exceeded.
read_first: desktop/src/components/EvaluationPanel.tsx (reference: existing manual revision loop pattern at handleRunAutonomousRevision lines 909-952)
desktop/src/api/agents.ts (reference: agent API surface — agentWrite, agentRevise)

criteria: grep -r 'revision-orchestrator' src-ts/src/mcp/ finds the endpoint registration
convergence.verification: Import RevisionOrchestrator in a test, call run() with mock text, verify it iterates and converges. Call MCP endpoint with test payload, verify response structure.
convergence.definition_of_done: Autonomous multi-pass revision works end-to-end: text goes in, orchestrator evaluates/revises in a loop, returns final text with score improvement metrics.

files.change: New file: RevisionOrchestrator class with run() method implementing evaluate→revise→verify loop
Unit tests for RevisionOrchestrator: convergence, max iterations, score degradation revert
POST /agent/revise-multi-pass accepting { text, target_score, max_iterations, workspace } returning { revised_text, iterations, initial_score, final_score }

implementation: Create src-ts/src/agents/revision-orchestrator.ts with interface RevisionOrchestratorConfig { targetScore: number (default 8.0); maxIterations: number (default 5); workspace?: ProjectWorkspaceContext }

Implement run(initialText: string) method: (1) Store initial text and create checkpoint, (2) Loop: evaluate current text via existing evaluation pipeline, (3) If score >= targetScore → break with success, (4) Select top suggestion, call revision API with suggestion as prompt, (5) Re-evaluate revised text, (6) If score degraded from previous → revert to previous text and break, (7) Update current text, (8) After max iterations, return best result
Return type: { completed: boolean; revisedContent: string; iterations: number; initialScore: number; finalScore: number; reason: string; history: Array<{iteration, score, suggestion}> }
Create MCP endpoint /agent/revise-multi-pass that accepts { text, target_score?, max_iterations?, workspace? } and delegates to RevisionOrchestrator
Register endpoint in MCP server setup (follow pattern from src-ts/src/mcp/endpoints/chat.ts)
Write unit tests: mock evaluation returning incremental scores, test convergence at target, test max-iterations stop, test score-degradation revert

unit: revision-orchestrator.test.ts: convergence stops when target reached
integration: MCP endpoint /agent/revise-multi-pass returns valid response structure

reference.pattern: Existing RevisionOrchestrator in desktop/src/services/revisionOrchestrator.ts — mirror the interface but implement as backend service
reference.examples: handleRunAutonomousRevision in EvaluationPanel shows the full UI-driven loop

rationale.chosen_approach: Backend-first orchestrator decoupled from UI state, following the gap recommendation to create a dedicated service managing text buffer and loop state without depending on React hooks or global stores.
decision_factors: Analysis gap: current revision loop is manual and UI-driven
Safety: checkpoint-based revert prevents quality degradation
Performance: backend execution avoids React re-renders during long loops
rationale.tradeoffs: Backend orchestration means longer round-trip for progress updates, but eliminates UI coupling

risks: LLM API calls may be slow for long revision loops — mitigate with configurable iteration count
Quality convergence not guaranteed — mitigate with score degradation detection and revert
